issues.description: Field StockIngredient.price has conflicting declared types across artifacts. The problem statement UML declares StockIngredient.price as int (problem_statement.md), and the provided solution uses an int field and an int getPrice() (solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java). The template repository's StockIngredient declares the price field and constructor parameter as double and exposes getPrice() returning double (template/src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java). This mismatch (double vs int) is inconsistent with the problem signatures (e.g., acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) and calculateTotalPrice returning int) and can force students to add casts or change types unexpectedly.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the price type consistent across all artifacts. Preferably change the template implementation to use int for the price field, constructor parameter, and getPrice() return type to match the UML and the solution (update 'private final double price' -> 'private final int price', constructor parameter type, and getPrice()). Alternatively, if fractional prices are intended, update the problem statement UML and the solution to use double and adjust method signatures/documentation accordingly (including acceptSupplyDelivery parameter types and calculateTotalPrice return type).

issues.description: The assignment identifier/title in the problem statement does not match the rootProject.name set in the provided repositories. Problem statement title: 'H02E02 - Panic at Seal Saloon' (problem_statement.md line 1). Template settings.gradle sets rootProject.name = 'H04E01---Panic-at-Burger-House' and the solution settings.gradle sets rootProject.name = 'H04E01---Panic-at-Burger-House-Solution'. This inconsistency can confuse students about which repository corresponds to the described exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a consistent project identifier across the problem statement and repository metadata. Update rootProject.name in both template and solution settings.gradle files to match the problem title (for example, 'H02E02---Panic-at-Seal-Saloon'), or update the problem statement title to reflect the repository names. Ensure both template and solution use the same rootProject.name to avoid confusion.
